title: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Tier Classification Guide
content:
Every Fire & Smoke Mitigation job is held at one of six tiers. Each tier has an entry gate made of the smoke severity found on the safety walk, the type of property at the loss address and, for two tiers, the affected floor area scoped on arrival. The three readings are part of the job record from dispatch.

## Entry gates

| Rank | Tier | Smoke severity | Property types | Affected area |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Smoke Odor Response | odor only | single-family home, condominium unit, multifamily unit | no area condition |
| 2 | Light Smoke and Soot Cleanup | light | single-family home, condominium unit, multifamily unit | no area condition |
| 3 | Moderate Fire and Smoke Cleanup | moderate | single-family home, condominium unit, multifamily unit | no area condition |
| 4 | Heavy Fire Cleanup | heavy | single-family home, condominium unit, multifamily unit | 2499 square feet or less |
| 5 | Structural Fire Large Loss | heavy | single-family home, multifamily unit | 2500 square feet or more |
| 6 | Commercial Fire Large Loss | moderate or heavy | commercial | no area condition |

The four severity readings are odor only, light, moderate and heavy. The four property types are single-family home, condominium unit, multifamily unit and commercial property. A gate is met only when every column of its row is met.

## Reading the gates

- Odor only, light and moderate severity on a residential property (single-family, condominium or multifamily) each lead to exactly one tier, ranks 1 to 3, whatever the affected area.
- Heavy severity on a residential property is split by area: up to and including 2499 square feet the gate of Heavy Fire Cleanup is met; from 2500 square feet the gate of Structural Fire Large Loss is met, but that gate lists only single-family homes and multifamily units.
- A commercial property meets the gate of Commercial Fire Large Loss when its severity is moderate or heavy; area plays no part in that gate.

## Worked classifications (hypothetical jobs)

| Hypothetical job | Severity | Property | Area | Gate met |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | heavy | single-family home | 2499 sq ft | Heavy Fire Cleanup |
| B | heavy | single-family home | 2500 sq ft | Structural Fire Large Loss |
| C | heavy | multifamily unit | 1800 sq ft | Heavy Fire Cleanup |
| D | light | condominium unit | 3200 sq ft | Light Smoke and Soot Cleanup |
| E | moderate | commercial property | 900 sq ft | Commercial Fire Large Loss |
| F | moderate | multifamily unit | 2600 sq ft | Moderate Fire and Smoke Cleanup |

Jobs A and B sit on either side of the area boundary: 2499 square feet is the last area inside the Heavy Fire Cleanup gate and 2500 square feet is the first area inside the Structural Fire Large Loss gate. Job D shows that area does not move a light-severity job, and job F that it does not move a moderate-severity residential job.

## Rank

The rank runs from 1 for Smoke Odor Response to 6 for Commercial Fire Large Loss and orders the tiers in the Fire & Smoke Mitigation schedules; it states no rule of its own.
